subject: Delhi monsoon rainfall, season to date
_why_this_file_exists: THE HOMEPAGE HERO'S MONSOON SLIDE HAD NO DATASET AT ALL. Its figures were typed into public/_pages/v3/home.html and followed nothing, which is how they came to contradict each other (see _unresolved below). Every other hero slide reads a committed dataset; this one now does too, so there is ONE place to correct it.
_not_automated: IMD IS NOT WIRED, AND THAT IS A PRIOR DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. home.html's own note records it: scraping IMD was rejected in August as brittle and legally doubtful. So unlike air (a live CPCB route), yamuna, heat, fire and forest loss (scripted fetches), this file is MAINTAINED BY HAND. The daily data-refresh workflow cannot update it and does not pretend to. If an IMD or IMD-derived API is ever wired, this file becomes a fetch target and the note goes.
_unresolved: THE SLIDE CONTRADICTED ITSELF IN TWO PLACES AND THIS FILE DOES NOT GUESS WHICH IS RIGHT. Found on 22 August 2026 while making the hero data-driven: (1) the reading is stated as 501 mm in the screen-reader sentence and as 512 mm in a source comment on the same slide; (2) the seasonal normal is stated as 396 mm in the screen-reader sentence and as 434 mm in the limit line directly below it. Nothing in this repository can settle either pair, and inventing a figure is forbidden. So `normal_mm` is null and the build refuses to inject a normal until the owner supplies the IMD figures with a date. The reading is carried as 501 because that is the number the slide actually renders and the one a reader sees.

reading.note: Above normal is not the same as illegal, so this slide does not turn red for it.

source.name: India Meteorological Department
source.how: Read by hand from IMD's published rainfall statistics. No API and no scrape — see _not_automated.

limit.label: No legal threshold.
limit.why: No statute sets a permitted rainfall, so nothing here can be over a limit. The comparison is against the seasonal normal, which is a climatological average and not a rule.
